In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Ar-Rahman.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The Most Gracious﴾ ﴿Taught the Qur'an﴾.

Some of the people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) said: This verse was revealed when the disbelievers ignored (tajahhala) ar-Rahman, may He be majestic and exalted, as Allah related of them in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Gracious," they say, "And what is the Most Gracious?"﴾ [Al-Furqan: 60], as has already been mentioned in Surat al-Furqan.

We have already presented the meaning of ar-Rahman and its evidences from the verses in the beginning of Surat al-Fatihah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created man﴾ ﴿and taught him eloquent speech (al-bayan)﴾.

Know first that the creation of man and His teaching him al-bayan are among the most dazzling signs of Allah, as He, exalted is He, indicated by His saying at the beginning of An-Nahl: ﴿He created man from a drop of fluid, and behold, he is an open adversary﴾ [An-Nahl: 4] (p-490) and His saying at the end of Ya-Sin: ﴿Does man not see that We created him from a drop of fluid, and behold, he is an open adversary?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77].

So man was yesterday a drop of fluid, and today he is in the utmost of eloquence and in severe contention, disputing concerning his Lord and denying His power to resurrect. The tremendous contrast between the drop of fluid and clarity in contention, together with the fact that Allah created him from a drop and made him a clear adversary, is one of His signs, exalted is He, indicating that He alone is the one worthy of worship and that resurrection from the graves is true.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse ﴿He created man﴾ does not here explain the stages of his creation, but He explained them in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He, in Al-Mu'minun: ﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop [of fluid] in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then made the clot into a lump, then made the lump into bones, then We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 12-14]. The verses explaining the stages of human creation are many and well known.

We have already explained the rulings relating to man in all his stages before birth at the beginning of Surah Al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection, then indeed, We created you from dust﴾ [Al-Hajj: 5] and the rest of the verse, and we explained there the meaning of nutfah, 'alaqah and mudghah linguistically.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse ﴿taught him al-bayan﴾: the verification regarding it is that what is meant by al-bayan is the expression of what is in the heart (al-damir).

What this noble verse indicates, that He taught man al-bayan, has come clarified in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and behold, he is an open adversary﴾ in Surah An-Nahl [An-Nahl: 4] and Ya-Sin [Ya-Sin: 77]. His saying "mubin" (open) may be understood as the active participle of the transitive "abana," with the object omitted for generality, meaning: clarifying everything he wishes to make clear and manifest by his tongue of what is in his heart; this is because his Lord taught him al-bayan. It may also be understood as an attributive adjective (sifah mushabbahah) from the intransitive "abana," meaning: "clear in contention," i.e., its manifestness is evident; and likewise, since he was not clear in contention except because Allah taught him al-bayan.

Allah, exalted is He, has bestowed favour upon man by making for him the instrument of al-bayan, which is the tongue and the two lips, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did We not make for him two eyes? And a tongue and two lips?﴾ [Al-Balad: 8-9].

(p-491) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The sun and the moon are by a reckoning.﴾

Al-Husban (الحُسْبان) is a verbal noun (masdar) to which the alif and nun have been added, just as they were added in al-Tughyan (transgression), al-Rujhan (preponderance), and al-Kufran (ingratitude). So the meaning of bi-husbanin is: by calculation and measure, from the Almighty, the All-Knowing. This is also among the signs of Allah and among His blessings upon the children of Adam, because by it they know the months, the years, and the days, and they know the month of fasting, the months of Hajj, the day of Jumu'ah, and the number of the women whose waiting period is counted in months, such as the woman who has despaired of menstruation, the young girl, and the woman whose husband has died.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse is clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a light, and determined for it stations, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. Allah did not create that except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.﴾ [Yunus: 5].

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, that you might seek bounty from your Lord and that you might know the number of years and the reckoning.﴾ [al-Isra': 12].

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate themselves﴾.

The scholars differed over what is meant by "the star" (al-najm) in this verse. Some scholars said: "The star" is that which has no stem among plants, such as herbs and greens, and "the tree" is that which has a stem. Other people of knowledge said: "The star" means the stars of the sky.

His commentator, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: What appears to me to be correct is that "the star" means the stars of the sky. The evidence for this is that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, in Surat al-Hajj explicitly mentioned the prostration of the stars of the sky and of the tree, and He did not mention in any verse of His Book the prostration of what has no stem among plants specifically. By the verse of al-Hajj we mean His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees﴾ [al-Hajj: 18], and the rest of the verse.

This verse indicates that the prostrating "tree" in the verse of ar-Rahman is the celestial stars mentioned together with the sun and the moon in Surat al-Hajj. The best way to explain the Qur'an is by the Qur'an. According to this view that we have chosen, "the star" means the stars (plural). We have already discussed this at the beginning of Surat an-Najm (p-492) and at the beginning of Surat al-Hajj, and we mentioned that among the Arabic evidences for the use of "najm" (star) to mean the stars is the saying of ar-Ra'i:

*So she began counting the stars, in a shelter, swiftly, by the hands of those eating, their dryness*

And the saying of Amr ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Makhzumi:

*They displayed her like a gazelle walking proudly, among five maidens, peers of one age.*
*Then they said, "Do you love her?" I said, in haste, "As many as the stars, the pebbles and the dust."*

As for His saying in this noble verse, "yasjudan" (they both prostrate), we have already discussed it fully in Surat ar-Ra'd, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows at the mornings and the evenings﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 15].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 7:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the heaven He raised high, and He set up the balance﴾.

As for His saying ﴿And the heaven He raised high﴾, we have already explained the verses that clarify it in Surat Qaf, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not looked at the heaven above them, how We built it and adorned it?﴾ and the verse that follows [Qaf: 6].

As for His saying ﴿and He set up the balance﴾, we have already presented the discussion of it in Surat ash-Shura, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth and the balance﴾ and the verse that follows [ash-Shura: 17].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And establish the weight with justice, and do not make the balance deficient.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And give full measure and full weight with justice; We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾ [al-An'am: 152], and we mentioned part of it in Surah ash-Shura.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 55, verse 10 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth He has set for all creatures﴾ ﴿Therein is fruit, and palm trees with sheaths﴾ ﴿And grain with husk, and fragrant plants﴾.

In this verse, exalted is He, mentions that He set the earth for the *anam*, which means creation, because the earth's being set for them in this magnificent form, receptive to every kind of benefit, such as the flowing of rivers, the digging of wells, the planting of grains and fruits, the burial of the dead, and other kinds of benefits, is among the greatest signs and the most important favours, which are the blessings. For this reason He said after it: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 13].

What this noble verse includes of His bounty, exalted is He, upon His creation by setting the earth for them with its benefits, and making it a sign for them, pointing to the perfection of their Lord's power and His right to be worshipped alone, has come clarified in many verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying: ﴿And it is He who spread out the earth and placed therein firm mountains and rivers, and from all fruits He made therein two mates, two﴾ up to the end of the verse [Ar-Ra'd: 3].

And His saying: ﴿It is He who made the earth tame for you, so walk through its regions and eat of His provision﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-Mulk: 15].

• And His saying: ﴿And the earth, after that He spread it out. He brought forth from it its water and its pasture. And the mountains He set firm﴾ ﴿as provision for you and your cattle﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 30–33],
• And His saying: ﴿And the earth – We spread it out, and how excellent are the spreaders﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 48],
• And His saying: ﴿He who made the earth a bed for you﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-Baqarah: 22].

And His saying: ﴿And the earth – We spread it out and cast therein firm mountains, and caused to grow therein of every beautiful pair﴾ ﴿as an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾ ﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water﴾ up to the end of the verse [Qaf: 7].

And His saying: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 29]. The verses of this kind are many and well known.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Therein is fruit﴾ means many kinds of fruits. We have already mentioned that this is a well-known Arabic style, and we have clarified it with verses and the speech of the Arabs.

His saying: ﴿And palm trees with sheaths﴾. *Dhat* means "possessing." *Al-akmam* is the plural of *kimm*, with a kasra on the kaf, and it refers to what appears of the palm tree at the beginning of its fruiting, shaped like a tongue, and then it splits open to release the blossom. It has been said that it is its fibre. Ibn Jarir chose that it includes both meanings.

His saying: ﴿And grain﴾ is like wheat and the like.

His saying: ﴿With husk﴾. Most scholars said: *al-'asf* is the leaves of the crop. From this is His saying: ﴿So He made them like eaten-up husk﴾ [Al-Fil: 5]. It has also been said that *al-'asf* is chaff.

His saying: ﴿And fragrant plants.﴾ The scholars differed about its meaning. Some people of knowledge said it is everything of the plant whose scent is pleasant and which is smelled for enjoyment of its fragrance. Some scholars said *ar-rayhan* is provision, and from this is the saying of al-Najm ibn Tawlab al-'Ukli:

*Thus the breath of God, His sweet fragrance, His mercy, and the bright clouds*
*A cloud that sends down the provision of the servants, reviving the lands and making the trees fragrant.*

The meaning of *ar-rayhan* as "provision" is required according to the qira'a (recitation) of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i. As for the recitation of others, it may carry both of the mentioned meanings.

The explanation of this is that this verse was recited by Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and 'Asim: ﴿And grain with husk, and fragrant plants﴾ with a damma on the ba', the dhal and the nun of the three words, and it is coordinated with *fakihah* (fruit), meaning: "Therein is fruit, and therein is grain…" etc. Ibn 'Amir recited it: *"wal-habba dha al-'asfi war-rayhan"* [with a fatha on the ba', the dhal and the nun of the three words], and in the Syrian Mushaf the written form is *dha al-'asfi* with an alif after the dhal in place of the waw. The meaning according to his recitation is: "And He created the grain with husk and the fragrant plant." According to these two recitations, *ar-rayhan* can carry both of the mentioned meanings.

The recitation of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i has a damma on the ba' in *al-habb*, a damma on the dhal in *dhu al-'asf*, and a kasra on the nun of *ar-rayhan*, coordinated with *al-'asf*. On this reading, *ar-rayhan* cannot mean the scented plant, because the grain, which is wheat and the like, possesses husk, which is leaves or chaff, and it is not something possessing a pleasant scent.

Thus on this recitation it is necessary that *al-'asf* means what cattle eat of leaves and chaff, and *ar-rayhan* means what people eat of the grain itself. The verse with this meaning is like His saying: ﴿As provision for you and your cattle﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 33], and His saying: ﴿So We bring forth by it crops, of which eat their cattle and themselves﴾ [As-Sajdah: 27].

And His saying: ﴿So We brought forth by it pairs of various plants﴾ ﴿Eat and graze your cattle﴾ [Ta-Ha: 53–54], and His saying: ﴿For you from it is drink, and from it are trees in which you pasture﴾ ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives…﴾ up to the end of the verse [An-Nahl: 10–11].

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Therein is fruit﴾: His mention in it of the bounty of fruits, which are of many kinds, has come clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying in Surah Al-Falah (the Believers): ﴿For you therein are many fruits, and from them you eat﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 19], and His saying: ﴿And fruit and pasture﴾ [Abasa: 31], and other verses.

What He mentioned here of His bounty in grain has come clarified in other verses:
• such as His saying: ﴿So We caused to grow thereby gardens and grain of the harvest﴾ [Qaf: 9],
• and His saying: ﴿So We caused to grow therein grain﴾ ﴿and grapes﴾ [Abasa: 27–28], and His saying: ﴿And We brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 33],
• and His saying: ﴿We bring forth from it green stalks, with clusters piled up﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-An'am: 99],
• and His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ [Al-An'am: 95],
and other verses.

What He mentioned here of His bounty in palm trees has come clarified in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿And the palm trees, tall, having spathes piled one upon another﴾ ﴿as provision for the servants﴾ [Qaf: 10], and His saying: ﴿Then We produced for you thereby gardens of palms and grapes﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-Mu'minun: 19]. Verses of this kind are many and well known.

What He mentioned here of His bounty in *ar-rayhan* as being provision, as in the recitation of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, has come clarified in many verses also:
• such as His saying: ﴿He it is who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ [Ghafir: 13],
• and His saying: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth?﴾ [Yunus: 31],
• and His saying: ﴿Or who is it that provides for you if He withholds His provision?﴾ [Al-Mulk: 21],
• and His saying: ﴿And He shaped you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things﴾ up to the end of the verse [Ghafir: 64].
Verses of this kind are many and well known.

* * *

**Issue:**

Some scholars of *usul al-fiqh* (the principles of jurisprudence) derived from this noble verse and similar verses, such as His saying: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 29], that the original ruling regarding what is on the earth is permissibility (*al-ibahah*), until a specific proof of prohibition comes. This is because Allah conferred a favour upon creation by setting the earth for them, and made for them therein their provisions of sustenance and fruit, in this verse of Ar-Rahman, and He conferred a favour upon them that He created for them all that is on the earth in His saying: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾.

It is known that He, exalted is He, does not confer favour by something prohibited, since there is no favour in a forbidden thing. They also argued for this by the restriction of prohibited things to specific items in verses of the Book of Allah,
• such as His saying: (p. 496) ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, except that it be carrion, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-An'am: 145],
• and His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-A'raf: 33],
• and His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-An'am: 151].

There are two other opinions on this issue:

The first: that the original ruling regarding what is on the earth is prohibition until a proof shows permissibility. They argued for this by saying that all things belong to Allah, exalted is He, and the original principle regarding the property of another is to prohibit dealing with it except with his permission. There are well-known discussions on this in the principles of jurisprudence, and this is not the place to expand on them.

The second opinion: it is suspension (*al-waqf*), without judging it as prohibited or permitted, until a proof is established. So the issue has three positions: prohibition, permissibility, and suspension.

His commentator, may Allah pardon and forgive him, said: What appears to me as correct in this issue is the detailed distinction, because the entities Allah created on the earth for people have three states:

The first: that there is benefit in it that is not mixed with harm, such as kinds of fruits and others.

The second: that there is harm in it that is not mixed with benefit, such as eating deadly poisonous herbs.

The third: that there is benefit from one aspect and harm from another. If it contains benefit not mixed with harm, then the correct view is to place it under permissibility until a proof shows otherwise, due to the generality of His saying: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾, and His saying: ﴿And the earth – He set it for all creatures﴾ up to the end of the verse.

If it contains harm not mixed with benefit, then it is under prohibition, due to His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "There shall be no harm nor reciprocating harm."

If it contains benefit from one aspect and harm from another, then it has three states:

The first: that the benefit outweighs the harm.

The second: the reverse of this.

The third: that both are equal.

If the harm outweighs the benefit, or is equal to it, then it is prohibited, due to the hadith "There shall be no harm nor reciprocating harm," and because averting corruptions takes precedence over securing benefits. If the benefit outweighs, then permissibility is more apparent, because what is established in the principles is that a superior benefit takes precedence over an inferior harm, as indicated by the author of *Maraqi al-Su'ud* in his saying:

*Disregard it if the corruption is further away, or give preference to reform, like captives who are ransomed with what benefits the Christians.*
*And consider the hanging of grapes [of the vine] in every east and every west.*

His meaning is: giving precedence to the superior benefit over the inferior or distant harm, illustrating it with two examples:

The first of them: that the release of Muslim captives from the hands of the enemy by ransom is a superior benefit, which takes precedence over the inferior harm, which is the enemy's benefit from the money paid to them as ransom for the captives.

The second: that people's benefit from grapes and raisins is a superior benefit over the harm of pressing grapes for wine. No one has said that grapes should be removed from the world to avert the harm of pressing wine from them, because benefiting from grapes and raisins is a superior benefit over that harm. This distinction that we have chosen has been indicated by the author of *Maraqi al-Su'ud* in his saying:

*The ruling is that by which the Law comes, and the origin of everything that causes harm is prohibition.*

* * *

**Note:**

Know that the scholars of *usul al-fiqh* say: a person is not prohibited from doing something except by a proof from the Law. They say that the proof for this is rational, namely the well-known original exemption, known as *al-ibahah al-'aqliyyah* (rational permissibility), which is the continuation of the original state of non-existence (of prohibition) until a transmitted proof removes it.

We say: verses from the Book of Allah have indicated that presumption of original non-existence (istishab al-'adam al-asli, the principle of presuming continuity of the original state) before the arrival of a transmitting textual proof is a valid argument regarding permissibility. Among this is that when Allah revealed His severe prohibition of riba (usury) in His saying, ﴿So if you do not do it, then be informed of a war from Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 279], and there were at the time of its revelation among them wealth acquired from riba, which they had earned before the prohibition was revealed, Allah explained to them that what they had done of riba, under the original state of freedom from obligation before the prohibition was revealed, incurs no blame upon them for it, since (p-498) there is no prohibition except by declaration. This is in His saying, ﴿So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists, for him is what has passed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275]. His saying "what has passed" means what elapsed before the revelation of the prohibition.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying, ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾ [an-Nisa: 22], and His saying, ﴿And that you combine two sisters, except what has already passed﴾ [an-Nisa: 23]. The more apparent view is that the exception in both of them, in His saying "except what has already passed," is disjunctive (munqati'), meaning: but what has passed of that before the revelation of the prohibition is pardoned, because it was under the original state of freedom from obligation.

And among the clearest verses indicating this is His saying, ﴿And Allah would not mislead a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear﴾ [at-Tawbah: 115]. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ), when he sought forgiveness for his uncle Abu Talib after his death upon polytheism, and the Muslims sought forgiveness for their deceased polytheist relatives, Allah rebuked them in His saying, ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they should be relatives﴾ [at-Tawbah: 113], the verse in full. They regretted seeking forgiveness for them, so Allah made clear to them that their seeking forgiveness for them incurs no blame, because it occurred before the prohibition of it was declared. This is explicit in what we have mentioned.

We have already mentioned that adherence to the original state of freedom from obligation is also excused in matters of principles (usul al-din), in the discussion of His saying, ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15]. We explained there the statements of the scholars on this and clarified what has come in the Qur'anic verses concerning it. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾ ﴿and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire﴾.

Al-salsal (dry clay) is dry earth that produces a sound (salsalah), i.e., a noise when struck with something. It was also said: al-salsal is foul-smelling clay. Al-fakhkhar is baked clay. In this verse Allah mentions one stage of the stages of the dust from which He created Adam. He explained in other verses that He created him from dust, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 59],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then suddenly you are human beings dispersing﴾ [al-Rum: 20],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop﴾ [Ghafir: 67],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55].

(p-499)

We have already explained, in His saying ﴿Indeed, We created you from dust﴾ and His saying ﴿From it We created you﴾, that the meaning of their creation from it is the creation of their father Adam from it, because he is their origin and they are his offspring. Then Allah, may He be exalted, kneaded this dust with water so it became clay (ṭīn). For this reason He said: ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [al-Isra': 61], and He said: ﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12], and He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7], and He said: ﴿Or those whom We created? Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾ [al-Saffat: 11], and He said, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, I am creating a human from clay﴾ [Sad: 71]. Then He left this clay to ferment until it became black mud (ḥama' masnun), i.e., black clay whose smell has changed, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We certainly created man from dry clay of black mud altered in smell﴾ (the verse) [al-Hijr: 26]. He said, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, I am creating a human from dry clay of black mud altered in smell﴾ [al-Hijr: 28], and He said, concerning Iblis: ﴿He said, "I would never prostrate to a human whom You created from dry clay of black mud altered in smell"﴾ [al-Hijr: 33]. Al-masnun is said to mean "changed," it is said to mean "shaped," and it is said to mean "smooth." Then this clay dried and became salsal, as He says here: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾, and He said: ﴿And We certainly created man from dry clay of black mud altered in smell﴾.

Thus the verses confirm one another, and the stages of that dust become clear in them, as is not hidden.

His saying: al-jann, i.e., and He created the jinn, who is the father of the jinn. It was also said: he is Iblis. It was also said: he is an individual of the jinn.

In light of this, the alif and lam are for the genus. Al-marij is the flame that has no smoke in it. His saying "from fire" explains "marij," i.e., from a pure flame that originates from fire.

What this noble verse includes, that He, may He be exalted, created the jinn from fire, has been clarified in other places, such as His saying in al-Hijr: ﴿And We certainly created man from dry clay of black mud altered in smell. And the jinn We created before from the fire of scorching wind﴾ [al-Hijr: 26–27], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay"﴾ [Sad: 76].

We have already elaborated on this in surah al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except Iblis; he refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾.

We have already explained the discussion of this verse at the beginning of as-Saffat, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts﴾ [as-Saffat: 5].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾ ﴿between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who released the two seas, this one sweet and palatable, and that one salt and bitter, and placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition﴾ [al-Furqan: 53].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾.

Nafi' and Abu 'Amr read this word as "yukhraju" (يُخْرَجُ), with a dammah on the yaa' and a fathah on the raa', in the passive voice (mabniyyan lil-maf'ul). On this reading, "al-lu'lu'" (اللُّؤْلُؤُ, pearl) is the deputy subject (na'ib fa'il) of "yukhraju." The rest of the seven readers read it as "yakhruju" (يَخْرُجُ), with a fathah on the yaa' and a dammah on the raa', in the active voice (mabniyyan lil-fa'il). On this reading, "al-lu'lu'" is the subject (fa'il) of "yakhruju."

Know that a group of the people of knowledge said that what is meant by His saying in this verse, ﴿From them come forth﴾, is from their totality, which encompasses the salt sea. They said the verse uses the whole to mean a part, and that the pearl and the coral do not come forth from the salt sea alone, to the exclusion of the sweet water.

This view that they held regarding this verse, despite their great number and eminence, is undoubtedly false, because Allah has explicitly stated its opposite in Surat Fatir. And there is no doubt that whatever contradicts the Qur'an is false. That is in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet, palatable, pleasant to drink, and that one is salty and bitter. And from each you eat fresh flesh and extract ornaments which you wear﴾ [Fatir: 12]. The tanwin (nunation, التَّنْوِينُ) in His saying "min kull" (مِن كُلٍّ) is the tanwin of substitution (tanwin 'iwad), meaning "from each one of the sweet and the salt you eat fresh flesh and extract ornaments which you wear." These ornaments are the pearl and the coral, and this is something on which there is no dispute.

We have already clarified this in Surat al-An'am, in discussing His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-An'am: 130]. Al-lu'lu' is the large pearl, and al-marjan is the red bead. Some of them said: al-marjan is the small pearls, and al-lu'lu' is the large ones.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 24:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And His are the ships, raised high upon the sea, like landmarks.﴾

(p-٥٠١) We have already discussed this in surah ash-Shura, in the discussion of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs are the ships on the sea, like landmarks.﴾ [ash-Shura: 32].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ ﴿but the Face of your Lord will remain, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾.

What this noble verse contains, namely the perishing of everyone on the earth and the remaining of His Face, glorified and exalted be He, who is described as Owner of Majesty and Honour, has been clarified in other places in the Qur'an,

such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ [al-Qasas: 88],

and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And rely upon the Living who does not die﴾ [al-Furqan: 58],

and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185],

along with other verses.

The Face (al-wajh) is one of the attributes of Allah the Exalted, by which He described Himself. It is incumbent upon us to affirm what our Lord has affirmed for Himself and to believe in it, while maintaining complete transcendence (tanzih) above resemblance to the attributes of created beings.

We have explained this with great clarity, through the Qur'anic verses, in Surah al-A'raf and in Surah Muhammad (al-Qital). And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 33:

Allah's statement: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through. You will not pass through except with authority.﴾

We have already discussed this verse in surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of Allah's statement: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17]. There we also spoke about other verses which the ignorant interpret in the Book of Allah without their intended meanings, so there is no need to repeat it here.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 35:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-406) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Rahman

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿A flame of fire and molten brass will be sent against you both, and you will not be able to defend yourselves.﴾

It is not hidden what comes to the mind: that the sending down of the flame of fire, which is its blaze, and the brass, which is its smoke (or, according to another view, molten brass), and the absence of any defence against it, contain no favour upon the two weighty creations (jinn and humankind). And His saying to them: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 36] implies that the sending of the flame and the brass, and the absence of defence, are among the favours (ala') of Allah, that is, His blessings upon the jinn and mankind.

The answer is in two respects:

The first: The repetition of ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ is for emphasis (tawkid). He did not repeat it consecutively, because repeating it after each verse is better than repeating it in succession. And if it is for emphasis, there is no difficulty, because what is mentioned after that which is not among the favours emphasises what is mentioned after that which is among the favours.

The second aspect: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ is mentioned only after the mention of a blessing, an admonition, or a warning and intimidation, and all of these are among the favours of Allah, which none denies except an unbelieving obstinate person. As for the mention of blessing, this is clear.

As for admonition, because exhortation softens hearts so that they humble themselves and turn in repentance, the means that leads to this is among the greatest blessings. Thus it is evident that admonition is among the greatest favours.

As for warning and intimidation, like this verse, there is also in it the greatest blessing upon the servant, because his being warned in the abode of this world about the terrors of the Day of Resurrection is among the greatest blessings of Allah upon him.

Do you not see that if a traveller had before him a great ruin, and he was on the verge of falling into it without knowing of it, and someone came to him, informed him of it and warned him against falling into it, this would be a favour (yad) for him with him and a kindness for which he rewards him with the greatest reward?

(p-407) This last aspect is what the principles (usul) require, because it has been established in the science of usul that when a text admits of both emphasis (tawkid) and initiation (ta'sis), the principle is to interpret it as initiation rather than emphasis, because initiation carries an additional meaning that emphasis does not.

On this view, the repetition of ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ is with regard to the kinds of blessings mentioned before it: a favour, an admonition, or a warning.

You have known that all of them are among the favours of Allah. So what is mentioned after His blessings is like what is mentioned after His saying: ﴿And His are the ships raised high (in the sea) like mountains﴾ [al-Rahman: 24], and after His saying: ﴿From both of them emerge pearl and coral﴾ [al-Rahman: 22], because the ships, the pearls and the coral are among the favours of Allah as is self-evident. What is mentioned after an admonition is like what is mentioned after His saying: ﴿And when the sky is split open﴾ [al-Rahman: 37], and what is mentioned after a warning or intimidation is like what is mentioned after His saying: ﴿A flame of fire will be sent against you both﴾, and Allah knows best.

**Verse 37:** ﴿And when the sky splits open and becomes rose-red like red leather﴾.

He, the Majestic and Exalted, mentions in this noble verse that the sky will split apart on the Day of Resurrection, and that when it splits it will become rose-red like red leather (dihan). His words "warda" (rose-red) mean red, the color of the rose. His words "ka-l-dihan" (like red leather) have two well-known interpretations among the scholars:

The first: *al-dihan* is red leather (*al-jild al-ahmar*). On this reading, the meaning is that the sky becomes rose-red, having the color of the rose and resembling red leather in its hue.

(p. 502) The second: *al-dihan* is that with which something is oiled (*ma yuhdan bihi*), i.e., oil or ointment. Regarding this reading, scholars differ on whether *al-dihan* is the plural of *duhn* (oil) or a singular noun, since the Arabs call whatever is smeared with oil *dihan*, and it is singular. From this usage is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

*"As though they were two water-skins of a hasty traveler, well-soaked, not yet scalded with oil."*

The real difference between the two interpretations is this: on the view that *al-dihan* is red leather, Allah describes the sky at its splitting on the Day of Resurrection with a single attribute, redness, and likens it to the redness of the rose and the redness of tanned red hide.

Some scholars said: the heat of the Fire will reach it, so it will turn red from the intensity of the heat. Other scholars said: the original state of the sky is red, but because of its great distance and the barriers between it and us, eyes cannot perceive its red color as it truly is, and on the Day of Resurrection it will be seen in its true color.

As for the view that *al-dihan* is that with which something is oiled, Allah describes the sky at its splitting with two attributes: first, the redness of its color, and second, that it melts and becomes liquid like oil.

On the first view, we do not know of any verse in the Book of Allah that clarifies this verse, stating that the sky will turn red on the Day of Resurrection until it is like the color of red leather.

As for the second view, that it melts and becomes liquid, Allah has clarified this in another place, in His words in al-Ma'arij: ﴿Indeed they see it as distant﴾ ﴿but We see it as near﴾ ﴿on the Day when the sky will be like *al-muhl*﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 7–8]. *Al-muhl* is a melted substance on both views, whether we say it is the dregs of olive oil, which is its sediment, or we say it is what melts of iron, copper, or the like.

Allah has also made clear in al-Kahf that *al-muhl* is a melted substance resembling water, extremely hot, in His words: ﴿And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like *al-muhl* that scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place﴾ [al-Kahf: 29].

As for the view that "warda" (rose-red) is a comparison to a *kumayt* horse, which is a reddish horse whose redness changes with the seasons, so that its redness intensifies in one season, tends toward yellow in another, and toward dust-color in another: the meaning of the comparison being that the sky, when it splits, changes into various colors, is clearly far from the apparent meaning of the verse. The statement of one who said that it goes and comes (i.e., moves back and forth) has support in the Book of Allah, in (p. 503) His words: ﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾ [al-Tur: 9], but in my view it is not free from distance.

What Allah mentions in this noble verse concerning the splitting of the sky on the Day of Resurrection is explained in many verses, such as:

• His words: ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 1];

• His words: ﴿So on that Day the Inevitable will occur﴾ ﴿and the sky will split open﴾ [al-Haqqa: 15–16];

• His words: ﴿And on the Day the sky will be split open with clouds﴾ [al-Furqan: 25];

• His words: ﴿When the sky breaks apart﴾ [al-Infitar: 1]. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Qaf, in our discussion of His words: ﴿And there are no fissures in it﴾ [Qaf: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 39:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin.﴾

In this noble verse, He - exalted is He - mentions that on the Day of Resurrection He will not ask mankind or the jinn about their sins. He clarified this meaning in His saying in Surah al-Qasas: ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins.﴾ [al-Qasas: 78]

He - exalted is He - has also mentioned in other verses that He will question all people on the Day of Resurrection, the messengers and those to whom they were sent, as in His saying: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers.﴾ [al-A'raf: 6], and His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do.﴾ [al-Hijr: 92-93]

Verses from the Book of Allah have come clarifying the way of reconciling these verses, which one who is not learned may suppose contain a contradiction.

Know first that the questioning that is negated in His saying here, ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾, and His saying: ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾ [al-Qasas: 78], is more specific than the questioning affirmed in His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do,﴾ because that includes the generalisation of questioning about every deed, whereas the two verses before it negate questioning only about sins specifically. There are well-known ways of reconciling these verses among the scholars.

The first of them, which is what the Qur'an indicates, and which is the point of evidence for us here regarding the Qur'an explaining the Qur'an, is that questioning is of two kinds: one is questioning of rebuke and reproach, which is a type of punishment, and the second is questioning of inquiry and seeking information.

So the questioning negated in some verses is questioning of inquiry and seeking information, because Allah knows their deeds better than they themselves do, as He said: ﴿Allah has enumerated it while they have forgotten it﴾ [al-Mujadila: 6].

Accordingly, the meaning is: neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin in the manner of inquiry and seeking information, because Allah knows his sin better than he does.

The questioning affirmed in the other verses is questioning of rebuke and reproach, whether it concerns a sin or not. An example of their being asked about sins in the manner of rebuke and reproach is His saying: ﴿As for those whose faces turn black, "Did you disbelieve after your belief? So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106]. An example of being asked about something other than sin is His saying: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned. "What is wrong with you that you do not help one another?" Rather, today they are submissive.﴾ [al-Saffat: 24-26], and His saying: ﴿The Day they are pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent push. "This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic?"﴾ [al-Tur: 13-15], and His saying: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-An'am: 130].

As for the questioning of the buried infant girl in His saying: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾ [al-Takwir: 8], it does not contradict the verses negating questioning about sin, because she is asked for what sin she was killed, and this was not her sin. The purpose of questioning her is to rebuke and reproach her killer, because she herself says, "I had no sin," so the blame returns upon the one who killed her unjustly.

Likewise the questioning of the messengers: its purpose is to rebuke and reproach those who denied them, together with establishing the proof against him that the messengers had delivered the message to him. The remaining ways of reconciling the verses are not indicated by any Qur'an, and the subject of this book is explaining the Qur'an by the Qur'an. We have explained the rest in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" at the beginning of Surah al-A'raf.

We have already presented a portion of this blessed book in Surah al-A'raf, in discussing His saying: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers.﴾ [al-A'raf: 6]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 41:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks, so they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.﴾

His statement "by their marks" (bi-simahum): that is, by their distinguishing sign. The Qur'an has indicated that this sign is the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black. As for those whose faces turned black...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106, to the end of the verse]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah, their faces blackened﴾ [al-Zumar: 60]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. It is as if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night. They are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [Yunus: 27]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And faces that Day will be dust-covered, darkness covering them. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa: 40-42], because the meaning of His statement ﴿darkness covering them﴾ is that blackness rises over them and covers them, like black smoke. He, may He be exalted, said concerning the blueness of their eyes: ﴿And We will gather the criminals that Day, blue-eyed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102]. Nothing is more ugly and more disfiguring than the blackness of faces and the blueness of eyes. For this reason, when the poet wanted to revile the excuses of the miser in the worst and ugliest terms, he described them with the blackness of faces and the blueness of eyes, when he said:

"For the miser, regarding his wealth, there are excuses — blue-eyed, upon them are black faces."

And especially when blackness of the face is joined with dust-coloring of it, as in His statement: ﴿Upon them will be dust-coloring, darkness covering them﴾, for that increases its ugliness upon ugliness.

As for His statement, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿so they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾, we have already presented its explanation and the verses clarifying it in surah al-Tur, in the discussion of His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent pushing﴾ [al-Tur: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 43:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go around between it and scalding, boiling water.﴾

As for His saying: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny,﴾ we have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surat at-Tur as well, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [at-Tur: 14].

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding, boiling water,﴾ we have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surat al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads, by which whatever is in their bellies will be melted away﴾ and what follows it [al-Hajj: 19-20].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 55, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But for him who fears the standing before his Lord there are two gardens﴾.

We have already explained, in the introduction to this blessed book, that a verse may have two valid interpretations, each of which is supported by the Qur'an. We mention all of them, making clear that all of them are true. We have given many examples of this throughout this blessed book, and among them is this noble verse.

The clarification of this is that this noble verse has two well-known interpretations among the scholars, both of which are supported by the Qur'an.

The first: the meaning of His saying ﴿standing before his Lord﴾ is his standing before his Lord, so "maqam" is a verbal noun (ism masdar) meaning "qiyam" (standing). The doer of the action, according to this interpretation, is the fearful servant, and it is attributed to the Lord only because it occurs before Him. This interpretation is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from [its] desire, Indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 40–41]. His saying ﴿and restrained the soul from [its] desire﴾ is an indication that he feared the consequence of sin when he stands before his Lord, so he restrained his soul from its desires.

The second interpretation: the doer of the verbal noun in the mimi form, which is "maqam", is Allah, may He be exalted. That is, this servant feared Allah's standing over him, His watching over his deeds, and His recording of them against him. This interpretation is supported by the verses that indicate Allah's standing over all His creation and His recording of their deeds, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255];

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then is He who is standing over every soul in what it has earned [like those who associate others with Allah]?﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 33];

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair or recite of it any Qur'an or do any deed except that We are witnesses over you when you are involved in it﴾ [Yunus: 61], and so on, along with other verses.

We have previously discussed, in surah al-Ahqaf, in the commentary on His saying concerning the jinn: ﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you of your sins﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31], that His saying ﴿But for him who fears the standing before his Lord there are two gardens﴾, and His explicit mention of this as a favour to both mankind and the jinn in His saying ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [ar-Rahman: 47], is a Qur'anic text indicating that the believing jinn who fear the standing before their Lord enter Paradise.

Allah's saying: ﴿Reclining on couches whose linings are of brocade﴾.

We have already explained in Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿and that you may extract from it ornaments to wear﴾ [an-Nahl: 14], all the Qur'anic verses indicating that the people of Paradise enjoy silk of sundus (fine silk) and brocade (istabraq), and ornaments of gold and silver. We also made clear that all of this is forbidden to the males of this Ummah in the life of this world.
